body:
# the contributor audit of exposed-base and exposed-face potential transfer

Source: `candidate 400ac36c18f8c3ff`,
Sections 1--7. Verdict: PASS in its explicitly positive, full-dimensional
fiber scope. This is not a global deepest-base exposure theorem.

The isolation tilt is finite because the measured base set is finite,
every off-base exposing value is strictly negative, and all fibers are
compact. It proves equality of raw mixed depth with own ordinary depth
at every point of the exposed fiber, including arbitrary oblique caps.
At a global deepest source the ordinary maximum is therefore exactly Q.
Ordinary depth continuity follows from the compact unit-normal minimum
of a jointly continuous cap-volume function. Boundary points have depth
zero; the ordinary centroid provides the positive bound Gamma_d |K|.

Every globally critical cap through or containing this source captures
at least Q on the own fiber and hence exactly Q there and zero elsewhere.
Opposite own caps give Q<=|K|/2, excluding a purely integer critical cap.
The own source is interior, so translating a strictly containing cap to
it removes a positive-volume slab. Thus every attaining cap boundary
passes through the source, with a proper own cut.

The proper-cut differentiability proof by vertical interval integration
is valid without smoothness. The section-boundary exception has zero
relative measure; the relative interior of a section crossing the body
interior is contained in that interior. Bounded first-moment difference
quotients justify dominated convergence. For d=1 the transverse measure
is H_0 on one point and the derivative is the ordinary interval-length
derivative. Compactness of the active unit-normal set, positive proper
section areas, and the positive inactive gap justify the source-motion
separation proof that zero belongs to its convex hull. A finite positive
continuous-normal circuit follows by Caratheodory and deletion.

Every ordinary attaining section has centroid at the source by its
vanishing tangent-normal derivative. A common finite exposing tilt
strictly misses all other fibers, preserves the continuous circuit, and
makes the full mixed section centroid the actual source. It need NOT
balance full ambient normals; the source never claims that. The response
weights rho_j/S_j are well-defined and positive.

The potential [u.(x-y)+B ell(z)]_+ is convex at each fixed u, nonnegative,
and exactly zero on every off-base normal bundle for a single finite B.
On the own boundary it equals the radial support u.(x-y), which is
strictly positive because y is interior. Its denominator d|K| and
cap numerator dQ follow from divergence, with zero cut-plane flux.
A proper cut plane meets the own boundary in a surface-null set, so the
closed convention does not alter that integral. The identity therefore
holds for ANY nonnegative normalized mixture of critical caps, not just
one specific response normalization. Off-base boundary allocations are
annihilated exactly. This proves individual efficiency Q/|K|>=Gamma_d.

For an exposed base face F, restriction and finite exposing extension
prove equality with the actual face subfamily's raw depth. The potential
extension composes a convex function with an affine projection onto
aff F, adds B ell_F, and takes positive part. It agrees with the original
test on F and vanishes off F; the stipulated compact uniform boundedness
is exactly what supplies finite B. This is composition of a function,
not a coordinate transformation of the body or lattice. No Jacobian or
lattice-preservation assertion is required. On-face boundary allocations
remain exactly the same, while off-face ones vanish.

The proof handles singleton base sets, n=0, and d=1 as stated. It does
not make a surface-measure construction for d=0 or varying intrinsic
fiber dimensions, and does not assert that any global deepest base is
exposed in the full positive-base hull.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
